result.title: EvoVAU: Tool Evolution for Video Anomaly Understanding
result.summary: Video anomaly understanding (VAU) requires reasoning about event progression, interactions, and the contextual conditions that distinguish abnormal behavior from common activity across diverse scenes. Although video agents enable multi-round analysis, the predefined analytical operations may not adequately satisfy these diverse reasoning demands. In this paper, we present EvoVAU, a framework that evolves a reusable tool library for a frozen video solver. Guided by task outcomes and execution trajectories, an external proposer identifies potential limitations in the library and refines it, retaining task experience as analytical operations that can be reused across questions. Specifically, Cross-Version Contrastive Feedback guides tool refinement by combining current errors with paired execution trajectories from historical corrections and regressions. Adoption-Aware Selection accepts a candidate library only when overall development-set accuracy improves and corrections outnumber regressions among questions on which the solver invokes new or modified tools. Using a small development set, EvoVAU alternates tool refinement with candidate evaluation and selection. At test time, the evolved library remains fixed, with no further involvement from the proposer. Experiments on several VAU benchmarks demonstrate strong performance and the flexibility of the evolved library across anomaly domains.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EvoVAU，为冻结的视频求解器进化一套可复用工具库：外部提议器依据任务结果与执行轨迹发现问题并改写工具，用跨版本对比反馈结合历史纠错与退化轨迹，并以采纳感知选择在开发集上验证后固定工具库用于测试。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「候选操作须在整体准确率提升且纠错多于退化时才被采纳」的门控式工具增删机制，可能为 LVR 中何时新增或保留某种推理操作、如何用轨迹分配监督以供核查，但论文面向视频异常理解而非 latent 状态生成，联系较间接。
